description: Post-quantum cryptography decomposed. NIST PQC standardization. Lattice-based (Kyber/ML-KEM, Dilithium/ML-DSA, FALCON). Hash-based (SPHINCS+/SLH-DSA). Code-based (Classic McEliece). The threat (Shor's algorithm), the timeline, the migration patterns (hybrid schemes), the trade-offs.

sub_mechanisms.name: Shor_algorithm_threat
sub_mechanisms.definition: Quantum algorithm for factoring + discrete log. Polynomial time on sufficiently large quantum computer.
sub_mechanisms.why: Breaks RSA + ECC. Required quantum: ~2300 logical qubits for RSA-2048. Current state: ~1000 noisy physical qubits. ~10-20 years estimated to threat. Migration starting now.

sub_mechanisms.name: Grover_algorithm_threat
sub_mechanisms.definition: Quantum search. Halves effective key length of symmetric crypto.
sub_mechanisms.why: AES-128 → 64-bit security under quantum. AES-256 → 128-bit (still safe). Symmetric easier to upgrade than asymmetric.

sub_mechanisms.name: harvest_now_decrypt_later_attack
sub_mechanisms.definition: Adversary records encrypted traffic now; decrypts when quantum available.
sub_mechanisms.why: Long-term secrets vulnerable today. State secrets, medical records, etc. require PQ now. Forward secrecy doesn't help captured handshakes.

sub_mechanisms.name: lattice_based_crypto
sub_mechanisms.definition: Security from hard problems on lattices (LWE, Module-LWE, SIS). Foundation of most NIST PQ winners.
sub_mechanisms.why: Well-studied since 1996. Believed quantum-resistant. Compact compared to other PQ. Kyber, Dilithium, FALCON all lattice-based.

sub_mechanisms.name: ML_KEM_Kyber
sub_mechanisms.definition: NIST FIPS 203. Lattice-based KEM. 768-bit security at ~1.5 KB public key + ~1 KB ciphertext.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard PQ KEM. Cloudflare, Google deploying. Often paired with X25519 in hybrid mode for transition. NIST standardised August 2024.

sub_mechanisms.name: ML_DSA_Dilithium
sub_mechanisms.definition: NIST FIPS 204. Lattice-based signature. ~1.3 KB public key, ~2.5 KB signature for security level 2.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard PQ signature. Replaces ECDSA/Ed25519 in PQ context. Larger keys + signatures than classical; rapid verification.

sub_mechanisms.name: FALCON_compact_signatures
sub_mechanisms.definition: FN-DSA (FIPS 206). Lattice-based, compact signatures. ~700-byte sig vs Dilithium's 2.5 KB.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bandwidth-constrained use cases. Cost: complex implementation (floating point), harder to make constant-time. Adoption slower than Dilithium.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLH_DSA_SPHINCS
sub_mechanisms.definition: FIPS 205. Hash-based signature. Security from cryptographic hash function strength. ~8-50 KB signatures.
sub_mechanisms.why: Different mathematical foundation than lattice. Defence in depth: if lattice broken, hash-based still works. Cost: large signatures, slow signing. Used where signing rare.

sub_mechanisms.name: Classic_McEliece
sub_mechanisms.definition: Code-based KEM. ~250 KB public keys, fast operations. NIST alternate (not primary).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation 1978; well-studied. Massive public keys disqualify for many uses. Niche: embedded systems, long-term keys.

sub_mechanisms.name: hybrid_PQ_classical
sub_mechanisms.definition: Combine classical (X25519) + PQ (Kyber) key exchange. Shared secret = KDF(both).
sub_mechanisms.why: Transition strategy. If PQ scheme broken, classical still works (and vice versa). Used in Cloudflare, Apple deployments. Standard during transition period.

sub_mechanisms.name: NIST_PQC_timeline
sub_mechanisms.definition: Competition started 2016. Round 1 (2017) → 4 finalists (2022) → standardized (August 2024). Industry now migrating.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decade-long process. Provides confidence in scheme analysis. Migration: 5-10 years; deprecation 10-20 years. ECC continues until then.

sub_mechanisms.name: quantum_resistance_uncertain
sub_mechanisms.definition: PQ schemes believed quantum-resistant but new attacks possible. Some candidates broken late in competition (SIKE, Rainbow).
sub_mechanisms.why: Cryptanalysis ongoing. Hybrid + algorithm agility (easy swap) protect. Standards may evolve as analysis matures.

derivation_rules.name: PQ_migration_urgency_proportional_to_secret_lifetime
if: secret must remain confidential for N years
then: if N > estimated time to large quantum computer, migrate now
derivation_rules.why: Harvest-now-decrypt-later. 20-year secrets need PQ today; 1-year secrets can wait. Long-term: state secrets, medical records, intellectual property. Short-term: most TLS sessions.

derivation_rules.name: hybrid_schemes_safer_during_transition
if: a new PQ scheme is deployed
then: pairing with classical scheme protects against PQ-scheme break
derivation_rules.why: If PQ scheme broken (cryptanalysis advances), classical still secure. If classical broken (quantum arrives), PQ still secure. Belt + suspenders. Cost: slight overhead. Standard transition pattern.

derivation_rules.name: PQ_keys_larger_than_classical
derivation_rules.why: Kyber pubkey 1.5 KB vs X25519's 32 bytes. Dilithium signature 2.5 KB vs Ed25519's 64 bytes. SPHINCS+ 8-50 KB sig. Protocols designed for compact crypto need redesign.

derivation_rules.name: lattice_based_dominant_for_NIST_winners
if: NIST has selected primary PQ standards
derivation_rules.why: Kyber, Dilithium, FALCON all lattice. Decades of analysis, good performance, reasonable sizes. SPHINCS+ hash-based as backup (different foundation).

derivation_rules.name: algorithm_agility_required_for_future_breaks
then: future cryptanalysis break requires expensive migration
derivation_rules.why: RSA → ECC migration took 20 years. PQ migration in progress. Future migrations inevitable. Modern protocols (TLS) negotiate algorithms; specific code paths can be retired.
